name: Repoformer - Selective Retrieval for Repository-Level Code Completion
venue: ICML 2024 (International Conference on Machine Learning) - Oral (acceptance rate 1.5%). Proceedings: PMLR v235 (https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/wu24a.html). Preprint: arXiv:2403.10059 (v1 15 Mar 2024, v2 4 Jun 2024).
authors_affiliation: Di Wu (University of California, Los Angeles - UCLA), Wasi Uddin Ahmad, Dejiao Zhang, Murali Krishna Ramanathan, Xiaofei Ma (all AWS AI Labs). Work done with/at Amazon; code released under amazon-science.
paper_url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.10059 (DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2403.10059; DBLP journals/corr/abs-2403-10059). Proceedings: https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/wu24a.html . Project page: https://repoformer.github.io/
code_url: https://github.com/amazon-science/Repoformer (Apache-2.0; data + inference code + CrossCodeLongEval benchmark). Training code based on https://github.com/amazon-science/ContraCLM.
maintained_repo_url: N/A (single per-paper code repo; no maintained leaderboard or living paper list).
task_domain: code (repository-level code completion: line, API-invocation, code-chunk, and function-body completion in user repositories).
problem_setting: Offline, single-agent, supervised setting. The system completes one or more consecutive lines Y in a file given the in-file left context X_l, right context X_r, and the set of other repository files F. RAG follows the four-stage RG-1 pipeline of Zhang et al. 2023 (indexing, query formation, retrieval, generation). The central question is whether to retrieve cross-file context at all: the authors show retrieval helps only ~20% of instances and harms ~20%, so they make retrieval selective. Repoformer is a single code LM, fine-tuned via self-supervision, that serves simultaneously as (a) the selective-RAG policy (decides whether to retrieve by emitting a special token) and (b) the generation model. It is trained once on permissively-licensed repositories from the Stack and then frozen at inference. It can also act as a plug-and-play selective-retrieval policy in front of larger black-box generation models (StarCoderBase-7B/16B, Code Llama, CodeGen25, ChatGPT/gpt-3.5-turbo).
what_is_retrieved: Cross-file code snippets (code chunks): fixed-size spans of consecutive lines extracted from other files F in the same repository (CC = cc_1...cc_k). Not documentation, demos, or trajectories - purely in-repository code context.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: the target repository's own files, indexed per-repository as a static snapshot. No growing/episodic agent memory; the retrievable store is frozen per repository and does not grow during deployment.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking (k=10 most-similar code chunks). The retrieval set size is fixed; the novelty is at the per-instance decision level (retrieve k=10 vs retrieve nothing), governed by a learned self-evaluation policy. Not minimal-complete-set recovery nor precision-driven variable-k within retrieval.
cbr_cycle_coverage: Retrieve=yes (selective, self-triggered); Reuse=yes (retrieved chunks injected as prompt context for robust generation); Revise=no (no case adaptation/revision); Retain=no (no write-back). [Retrieve, Reuse] only.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False - the work frames itself as selective retrieval-augmented generation (selective RAG) / adaptive RAG for code; it does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner and does not present itself as case-based reasoning.
retrieval_unit: token/snippet: a fixed-size code chunk of consecutive lines (chunk size = 20 lines for line/API/chunk completion, 50 lines for function completion; stride = half the chunk size). After retrieval, fragment alignment (Lu et al. 2022) replaces each top chunk with the chunk immediately following it.
index_source: Static, offline-constructed per-repository store: all files in F are partitioned into fixed-size sliding-window code chunks at indexing time. No online/test-time induction or growth. (Training-data labels are induced offline by simulating RAG over 18k filtered Stack repositories.)
index_structure_topology: Flat similarity index over sliding-window code chunks within a repository (bag-of-tokens for Jaccard / dense vectors for UniXcoder). No dependency graph, knowledge graph, or hierarchical category structure.
retriever_type: Sparse lexical by default: Jaccard similarity over token sets (chosen for speed and strong performance, following Zhang et al. 2023). Also evaluated dense retrievers - UniXcoder cosine similarity and OpenAI-embedding cosine similarity (CCEval) - and CodeBLEU; Jaccard was not outperformed by these on the main tasks. The retriever itself is off-the-shelf (not trained).
retriever_learning_signal: none for the retriever (off-the-shelf Jaccard / UniXcoder / OpenAI embeddings, no training). The LEARNED component is the selective-retrieval POLICY inside the code LM: it is trained by self-supervised LM-feedback - the ground-truth retrieve/abstain label is obtained by contrasting the LM's own completion quality (Edit Similarity vs the ground truth Y) with vs without retrieval augmentation (label positive if retrieval improves ES by more than threshold T=0).
query_construction: The query to the in-repository retriever is formed from the in-file context (X_l and X_r). During training data creation, the target Y is additionally included in the query for 50% of instances (oracle-in-query), to align with both non-iterative and iterative use where a draft prediction Y' is used to re-query. The selective decision itself is made by the LM from X_l and X_r before any retrieval.
query_granularity: task-level / one-shot at the completion point: a single retrieval decision and (if triggered) a single retrieval is made for each completion instance after observing X_l, X_r. No multi-step / per-token re-querying (the paper notes single-iteration RAG already captures most gains of iterative RAG).
when_to_retrieve: adaptive (learned router) + one-shot: a learned self-evaluation policy decides per instance whether to retrieve once. Retrieval is selective rather than always-on; when triggered it is a single (one-shot) retrieval.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Learned self-assessment via a reflection-style token: after observing X_l, X_r the LM emits the end-of-current-file token <eof> and then predicts a special token <cc> (retrieve) or an empty token (abstain). In practice retrieval is triggered when p(<cc>) exceeds a threshold T (Threshold/SelectiveT, e.g. T=0.2 for line/API/chunk, T=0.15 for function) or greedily if <cc> is the most likely token (Greedy/SelectiveG). This single forward-pass signal jointly encodes (1) whether the LM already knows the answer (self-knowledge, a la Kadavath et al. 2022) and (2) whether cross-file info is likely needed. Contrasted with trial-retrieval (retriever similarity) and trial-generation (token-uncertainty/entropy) heuristics, which the paper shows are less effective and incur retrieval/generation latency.
reranking: No dedicated reranking stage. Top-k chunks are taken by retriever similarity; fragment alignment (use the following chunk) is the only post-retrieval reordering/transformation. No cross-encoder, RRF, or instruction-tuned reranker.
retrieved_context_refinement: Minimal: fragment alignment (replace each retrieved chunk with the immediately-following chunk, per Lu et al. 2022) and concatenation into the prompt up to the context budget. The key refinement is at the decision level (selectively NOT retrieving) plus training the LM for robustness to noisy contexts, rather than distilling/compressing/decomposing the retrieved text. No distractor-filtering module.
tool_document_engineering: N/A - no tools/skills/tool-docs; retrieved units are raw code chunks.
index_content_separation: N/A - no progressive-disclosure / lightweight-index-then-content separation; retrieved chunks are used directly.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A - no live tool index or integration protocol (no RapidAPI/RESTful/MCP/function-calling). Repository index is a static per-repo snapshot.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A - no inter-tool dependency modeling (no tools).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: if retrieval is triggered, the retrieved cross-file chunks CC are placed after the special token <cc> and concatenated with X_l and X_r in a fill-in-the-middle-style prompt; the same code LM then generates Y. If abstaining, the LM generates from X_l, X_r only. The selective decision and the generation are produced in a single left-to-right pass (an extension of fill-in-the-middle). Crucially, the framework also doubles as a training signal: a self-supervised multi-task objective (L_eval for the <cc> self-assessment + L_gen for code generation, total = lambda*L_eval + L_gen, lambda=1.0) teaches the LM both to self-trigger and to robustly use noisy CC.
planning_integration: retrieve-then-generate, gated by a self-triggered decision: there is no explicit planner/tree-search. The pipeline is: observe in-file context -> LM self-evaluates (one forward pass) -> optionally retrieve once -> LM completes. In the online-serving latency model, the decision (P1), no-retrieval generation (P2), and retrieve+generate (P3) are issued in parallel and the system keeps whichever the decision selects.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-answer / per-completion: a single self-assessment + at most one retrieval per completion instance; retrieval is not interleaved per CoT-step or per-token.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (not framed as CBR). Retrieved chunks are used as verbatim in-context augmentation; robustness to them is acquired via training rather than explicit case revision.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw code chunks (verbatim consecutive lines from other repo files), injected as plain in-context text after the <cc> token. No distilled strategy, workflow, program-skill, or latent representation.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw code (concrete, low-abstraction): contiguous code line spans from sibling files in the repository, akin to demonstration-style raw context rather than a distilled insight or guideline.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Retriever-aware / robustness-oriented fine-tuning: the self-supervised multi-task objective trains the LM to (a) abstain from retrieval when CC would not help or would harm (performance-oriented self-evaluation) and (b) robustly leverage potentially noisy CC when retrieved (L_gen conditions on CC for positively-labeled instances). Analyses (Figure 6) show Repoformer has fewer/smaller performance drops from CC than StarCoderBase, and robustness holds under dense retrieval with a different context distribution (Table 8). Labels are derived by contrasting the LM's own output quality, making it a distractor-/noise-aware SFT.
memory_type: none - no persistent episodic/skill/workflow memory. Uses a static per-repository code index plus the fine-tuned LM's parametric knowledge.
write_back: False - the system does not store new experiences/cases/skills at inference time. (Training data labels are mined offline once; nothing is written back during deployment.)
online_growth: False - the retrievable store is a frozen per-repository snapshot and the LM is frozen after fine-tuning; neither grows during deployment.
write_back_trigger: never - no write-back event at inference time.
failure_experience_usage: Not stored as runtime experience. During OFFLINE training-label creation, both helpful and unhelpful/harmful retrievals are used contrastively: an instance is labeled negative (abstain) when retrieval does not improve (or hurts) the LM's completion ES, and positive (retrieve) when it does. This success-vs-no-gain contrast is the supervision signal, but no failure cases are retained in an inference-time memory.
memory_evolution_update: N/A - no stored entries are mutated (no memory); the per-repo index is static.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Yes (partially): the WHEN-to-retrieve decision is a learned self-evaluation policy trained via self-supervised LM-feedback (contrastive ES labels) and applied through a threshold on p(<cc>). It is not an RL/value-based policy and the WHAT-to-retrieve step remains fixed similarity top-k; but the retrieval-gating decision is genuinely learned rather than a fixed similarity rule.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No cross-agent memory sharing. However, the learned selective policy generalizes across generation models: Repoformer-1B serves as a plug-and-play selective-RAG policy in front of heterogeneous larger LMs (StarCoderBase-7B/16B, CodeGen25-7B, Code Llama-7B/16B, ChatGPT), improving their accuracy while cutting latency ~25%.
benchmarks: RepoEval (Zhang et al. 2023; line completion: 16 repos / 1600 instances; API completion: 16 repos / 1600 instances; function completion: 16 repos / 455 instances, unit-test verifiable). CrossCodeLongEval (new benchmark introduced by this paper, built from 1500 raw Python repos from CrossCodeEval; chunk completion: 944 repos / 5000 instances; function completion: 1460 repos / 5000 instances). CrossCodeEval (Ding et al. 2023; line completion across Python, Java, C#, TypeScript) used for multilingual generalization.
benchmark_family: code (repository-level code completion: RepoEval / CrossCodeEval / CrossCodeLongEval family).
baselines: Primary comparisons (same generation model, StarCoder family): (1) No Retrieval (in-file X_l + X_r only); (2) Always Retrieving (single-iteration RG-1 RAG pipeline of Zhang et al. 2023, the state-of-the-art prompting baseline). Generation models compared/used as backbones: StarCoderBase-1B/3B/7B, StarCoder-16B, CodeGen-Mono-2B/16B, CodeGen25-7B, Code Llama-7B/16B, ChatGPT (gpt-3.5-turbo-0613). Selective-policy alternatives compared in appendices: trial-retrieval (retriever similarity score: BM25/sparse, UniXcoder, CodeBLEU) and trial-generation (token uncertainty / entropy) heuristics; conceptually contrasted with SKR (Wang et al. 2023) and Self-RAG (Asai et al. 2024).
key_metrics: Exact Match (EM), Edit Similarity (ES = 1 - Levenshtein/max-length, reported x100), and unit-test pass rate (UT) for function completion. Efficiency metrics: %RAG (fraction of instances where retrieval is performed) and Speedup (SU) vs always-retrieving. Decision-quality metrics: abstention precision and calibration of the selective decision.
headline_result: 16B Repoformer with threshold selective RAG sets state-of-the-art repository-level code completion, outperforming the strongest StarCoder-16B always-retrieving baseline by ~3% averaged across tasks; Repoformer outperforms same-sized StarCoderBase always-retrieving by more than 3 absolute ES points on multiple tasks, and Repoformer-3B matches/surpasses always-retrieving StarCoder-16B on several tasks. Efficiency headline: selective retrieval yields up to 70% inference speedup in online serving (with dense retrieval / large repos) without harming accuracy; threshold selection improves BOTH accuracy and latency vs always retrieving. Concretely (RepoEval, 1B, Table 3) SelectiveG reaches 18-19% %RAG with 61-69% speedup at ~1 ES drop; SelectiveT keeps/improves ES with 27-28% speedup.
ablations: Section 5.1 proof-of-concept: on RepoEval API/function completion, retrieval improves only ~20% of instances, leaves >60% unchanged, and HARMS ~20% - consistent across CodeGen-Mono 2B/16B, StarCoderBase-1B, StarCoder-16B (motivates selectivity). Section 6 ablations (StarCoderBase-1B): (A1) merging L_eval and L_gen into one cross-entropy down-weights L_eval so p(<cc>)~=1 and selective decisions become meaningless (always retrieves); (A2) removing L_eval slightly improves RAG accuracy but loses the selective ability (so L_eval adds selectivity at little RAG cost); (A3) further removing CC (pure fill-in-the-middle) matches in-file completion but degrades RAG performance, showing training-with-CC is necessary; (A4) placing <cc>/CC inside the fill-in-the-middle infilling span (marked by <cc_end>) badly hurts function completion by breaking pretrained FIM semantics. Other analyses: threshold insensitivity (T=0.4 still matches always-retrieving with 50% latency cut); abstention precision >0.8 on all tasks (0.78 for RepoEval function); robustness to dense vs sparse retrieval; generalization to Java/C#/TypeScript (Repoformer-M) and to larger black-box generation models.
evaluation_decoupling: Partial. End-to-end task metrics (EM/ES/UT) are the primary report. Intrinsic retrieval ranking metrics (Recall@k/nDCG) are NOT the focus; instead the paper decouples the DECISION quality (retrieval abstention precision and calibration of p(<cc>)) and the retrieval budget (%RAG) from end-to-end accuracy, and separately analyzes retrieval helpfulness distribution (Figure 3, Table 1).
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both. Outcome metrics: EM/ES/UT of the final completion. Process/decision metrics: precision of retrieval-abstention decisions (>0.8), calibration of the selective prediction, %RAG, and per-instance analyses of whether CC helps/harms - i.e., the quality of the intermediate retrieve/abstain decision is evaluated, not only final code correctness.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Central contribution. The selective decision costs only a single forward pass (T_d < T_g < T_r + T_g). Reported: SelectiveT gives 27-28% speedup with equal/better accuracy and SelectiveG 61-69% speedup at ~1 ES drop on RepoEval line/API (Repoformer-1B); as a plug-and-play policy for larger LMs, Repoformer-1B cuts latency ~24-32% while improving accuracy (Table 4). With dense retrieval on large repos (retrieval = >80% of pipeline latency) a ~20% RAG budget translates to >70% end-to-end speedup. Note: sparse retrieval on moderate repos is already as costly as 3B-LM generation, motivating the savings.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed k=10 retrieved code chunks when retrieval is triggered; chunk size 20 lines (line/API/chunk) or 50 lines (function), stride = half chunk size; max sequence length 2048 during fine-tuning; max generated tokens follow RepoEval conventions. The novel budget control is the per-instance binary gate set by threshold T on p(<cc>) (e.g. T=0.2 line/API/chunk, T=0.15 function), tuning the fraction of instances that retrieve (%RAG) and thus the accuracy-latency trade-off; k itself is fixed (not adaptive within retrieval).
benchmark_construction_and_size: CrossCodeLongEval (introduced here): built from 1500 raw Python repositories from CrossCodeEval by sampling new blanks (to avoid CrossCodeEval's bias of removing instances StarCoderBase-1B answers correctly without retrieval). Chunk-completion split: 944 repos / 5000 instances (avg |Y| ~1.47 lines / 19.2 tokens); function-completion split: 1460 repos / 5000 instances (avg |Y| ~9.5 lines / 111.2 tokens). Construction = algorithmic sampling of code chunks (Poisson-length) and function bodies + Jaccard RAG simulation; answer verifiability is reference-based (EM/ES) for chunk and reference-based for function (RepoEval function split is unit-test verifiable). Released with the code under Apache-2.0.
builds_on: RG-1 single-iteration RAG pipeline and RepoEval from RepoCoder (Zhang et al. 2023); fill-in-the-middle training (Bavarian et al. 2022); StarCoder/StarCoderBase (Li et al. 2023) and CodeGen/CodeGen25 (Nijkamp et al.) code LMs; LM self-knowledge / 'language models know what they know' (Kadavath et al. 2022); Jaccard / UniXcoder (Guo et al. 2022) retrieval and fragment alignment (Lu et al. 2022, ReACC); the Stack (Kocetkov et al. 2022) for training repos; ContraCLM (Jain et al. 2023) training infrastructure; CrossCodeEval (Ding et al. 2023).
contrasts_with: Always-retrieving RAG for code completion (RepoCoder/Zhang et al. 2023, and structured-context fine-tuned methods like RepoFusion/Shrivastava et al., CoCoMIC/Ding et al. 2024). Among adaptive-RAG works, explicitly contrasted with SKR (Wang et al. 2023, needs extra module + knowledge store of unhelpful instances) and Self-RAG (Asai et al. 2024, distills a smaller LM using GPT-4 oracle labels): Repoformer needs no extra module, no knowledge store, and no oracle-LM labels - it self-supervises from the LM's own contrastive output quality. Also contrasted with uncertainty-triggered RAG (Jiang et al. 2023 FLARE, Li et al. 2023) and trial-retrieval relevance gating (Drozdov et al. 2022), which the paper shows are less robust across completion lengths and incur retrieval/generation latency.
lineage: Group B (RAG for task-solving), code-domain selective/adaptive RAG. Direct descendant of RepoCoder (RG-1 / RepoEval) in repository-level code completion; introduces the code-domain 'when-to-retrieve' question, paralleling QA-domain adaptive/self-RAG (Self-RAG, SKR, FLARE, Adaptive-RAG) but powered by self-supervised contrastive ES labels rather than oracle-LM distillation. Predecessor to later selective/efficient repo-level RAG and RL-based code retrieval methods (e.g. RLCoder).
